tasks.source: JetBlue's real storm days at its JFK and Boston hubs, pack b6-v1, drawn from a pool covering 13 months between December 2022 and July 2025: the flights, tails and delays from BTS on-time data, passengers from T-100, aircraft from Form 41 B-43 and the FAA registry, hourly slot caps from what all carriers actually moved, and the FAA Command Center's advisories, METARs, TAFs and forecast discussions as issued
tasks.selection: 5 of the pack's 20 eval days, one run each: a first look picked by hand (b6-bos-20240107-0600, b6-bos-20250216-1500, b6-jfk-20230714-1400, b6-jfk-20240804-0700, b6-jfk-20250709-1500; 3 JFK and 2 Boston, 3 summer and 2 winter), not a random sample, and the plugin didn't record how they were chosen, so the mean is not an estimate over the 20. The 20 eval days: among the 60 (day, hub) pairs of most disruption, the window of 3 to 6 whole hours where doing nothing costs most over the hindsight optimum, among windows where every hub movement has a typed tail, weather and air traffic control (BTS causes B and C) caused at least 80% of the cancellations in scope and 30 to 80 aircraft are in play; kept when doing nothing costs at least 10% over the optimum, the follower lands within 15% of it and the optimum is proven within 60 s, at most one per date and hub

grading.reference: the hindsight optimum: the time-line MIP (HiGHS, 1-minute arcs) on the day as it really happened, proven to 0.01%
grading.reward: 0.2 + 0.8 exp(-g/0.5), g = max(0, cost - hindsight) / (hindsight - floor + 0.02 hindsight), the floor being the same MIP without aircraft routing; cost in passenger-minutes: arrival delay, 523 per cancelled passenger and the night's ferries; graded once, on the final plan flown on the day as it happened; a day is scored only if it finished and every watch's news arrived before the agent's next call; turns: 5 a watch plus 4 (64 to 104 on these days)
grading.excused: nothing: every cost is charged, including what news after a flight's last chance to change brings to it, and the env never strands a flight, so there are no rule breaks; the anchor knows every delay and cap in advance, so 1.0 is out of reach online: the follower (0.730 on these days) shows what re-planning online reaches

baselines.name: the follower: the time-line MIP re-solved at every watch on the day as known
the blind follower: the same with no forecast of what isn't known yet
naive: no plan, every flight as early as it can
the airline: JetBlue's own cancellations and departure times as the plan
